references: The racket is prepared late on the backhand side, so the shuttle is met behind the body and the clear falls short. Start the backswing as the opponent makes contact, not as the shuttle crosses the net.
Racket preparation is too slow on the backhand, meeting the shuttle behind the body and losing depth on the clear. Begin the backswing earlier, on the opponent's contact.
Recovery to the base position is incomplete after the net shot, leaving the rear court open. Push off the lunge immediately and take two recovery steps back towards centre.
After the net shot the player stays forward instead of recovering, exposing the rear court. Drive off the front foot and move back to base straight away.
The smash is hit flat with the arm alone and little body rotation, so it carries pace but no steep angle. Rotate the hips and shoulders through the shot and make contact further in front and higher.
There is no trunk rotation into the smash, producing a flat trajectory that is easy to defend. Turn the body through the shot and take the shuttle higher and earlier.
The split step is late, landing after the opponent has already struck the shuttle, which delays the first movement to the corners. Time the split to land just before their contact.
Split-step timing is late relative to the opponent's contact, costing a step towards the corner. Land the split just as they begin their forward swing.
The serve is struck from too low and too far behind the front service line, giving the receiver time to attack it. Contact the shuttle higher and stand closer to the line to flatten the trajectory.
The low serve is released from below the ideal contact point and lands short, letting the receiver step in and kill it. Take the contact higher and closer to the service line.
Defence is played with a flat racket face and a stiff wrist, so blocks pop up mid-court. Relax the grip and angle the face slightly downward to drop the block tighter to the net.
The defensive block sits up because the grip is tense and the face is square. Loosen the grip on contact and tilt the racket face down to keep the block low.

Footwork into the forehand rear corner uses a side shuffle rather than a scissor jump, arriving late and forcing a defensive lift. Use a scissor-kick take-off so the shuttle can be met in front and attacked.
The player shuffles into the rear forehand corner instead of scissoring, arriving behind the shuttle and having to lift. Adopt a scissor jump to attack from the back.
Shot selection is predictable: three consecutive cross-court clears from the same position let the opponent anticipate and move early. Mix straight drops and half smashes from the same preparation.
The player repeats the cross-court clear from an identical setup, so the opponent reads it and starts moving early. Vary the shot from the same preparation to disguise the intention.
